items.title: A one-dimensional point of a normalization outside the image of the source has discrete valuation ring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a finite type morphism with reduced source over a Nagata base, a one-dimensional point of the normalization lying outside the image of the source has discrete valuation ring (statement lines 14292-14302). The counted proof is a substantial argument: it reduces to a finite affine Noetherian situation with base equal to its normalization, uses prime avoidance to pick an element in the relevant prime but in no minimal prime, shows that the closure of the image of the vanishing locus of that element misses the point because only generic points specialize to a one-dimensional point, shrinks the base so that the vanishing locus disappears, and then reads normality of the local ring off the equality of the ring with its integral closure in a localization, using that the localization of a one-dimensional reduced ring is a product of fields (proof lines 14296-14348). It is H2: all reductions and the local computation are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard Nagata, prime avoidance and integral closure statements.
